title: DECISION: sender checks effective preference before calling Peer/receipt
description: The Peer/receipt Sender Behavior requires the sending server to determine the effective receiptSharing preference (chat-level override if present, else account-level) and suppress the outbound Peer/receipt call entirely if it is false. This is better than relying solely on the receiver to suppress the readAt. Defense-in-depth: the sender never transmits data the user opted out of sharing; the receiver also applies its own check. This matters because the receiver's suppression logic runs on the recipient's infrastructure, which the sender does not control. Sender-side enforcement ensures the opt-out is honored even if a receiver is buggy or non-conforming. It also avoids the unnecessary network round-trip and reduces the amount of timing metadata leaked by the protocol.
